items.quote:
I genuinely love this game. ️ 

I’ve never been a huge racing game fan, but there’s something about Star Wars Galactic Racer that just feels right.

The handling is incredibly smooth and intuitive, the story is great, the characters are brilliant, the planets look fantastic, and the sound design is insane, the soundtrack is brilliant!

There’s just so much this game gets right and I absolutely love the runs mechanic — such a cool addition to a racing game.I’m around 20 hours in and already Rank 40 in multiplayer, and I’m still having a blast.

Honestly, this game gets a perfect review from Biddy alone. ️

items.author: Leesan

items.quote: In many racing games, you might eventually feel like a pilot. But only in this one you become a Jedi. It is insane. I can't stop playing it. The sensation is indescribable. This game let the players play the story and feel what it is like to be behind those speed monsters. And when you get to control them, when you are going through those dark tunnels of death at more than 600, 800, 1,000km/h, at night, in a heavy rain, and when only the sudden lightnings briefly show the surrounding and the shapes so you have a millisecond to turn... only then you understand what it is to have the force be with you. This is a masterpiece. This is the best Star Wars game ever made because it is the only one that truly delivers the force. It is also one of the best racing games ever. This is one of my favourite games of all time.
items.author: eBITDA

items.quote:
This game is perfect!

It had been a long time since I felt motivated to play racing games, as this genre no longer seems to receive the same love and care it used to.

But then, out of nowhere, Star Wars: Galactic Racer arrives... and it's here to stay, ready to earn its place among the greats. Non-stop action and guaranteed fun.

A deeply crafted story mode built around a roguelite system that works flawlessly, with the same concept also making its way into multiplayer. I've barely been able to put the game down when playing with my friends.

An absolute gem.

items.quote: Extremely fun and addictive. The sense of speed is fantastic, and the game really captures that feeling of going ridiculously fast while still giving you enough control to master it. You can definitely feel the Burnout influence, especially in the aggressive, skill-based driving and the satisfaction of pulling off a perfect **** despite how accessible it feels, there’s a real skill ceiling here. Getting good actually takes practice, and mastering the tracks, handling and shortcuts is genuinely rewarding. A great mix of arcade fun and skill-based racing.

items.author: ThemOnions

items.quote: As someone who absolutely loves fast cars (I own a Corvette C7), racing games (ever since SNES F-Zero) and Star Wars ('nough said), I can honestly say this game is an absolute THRILL. It gives me the same kick & feel as putting the pedal to the metal in 460 hp of V8 steel: prepping your abilities before the race feels like flipping a NOS switch, starting your engine draws you into the race Phantom-Menace style, the sound of your jet engines, everything about this feels so **** then they've made an excellent choice by making this a roguelite, because what is the thrill of a racing game if you have nothing to lose?! They strike a perfect balance between risk & reward, tuneability, vehicle differences and handling, and a great choice again to keep pod racers for later, because it gives you something more and even faster to work towards. I haven't got there yet, but even the starting vehicles already feel so fast!The first time playing F-Zero back in 1995 (I was 9) was with a range of hovercraft, and that thrill is back, but now with modern technology and a hell of a lot more customisation. I have only completed Act I and II on Ace (the level I started), but to me this is already the best racing game I have ever played when it comes to the thrill of racing; not even the most expansive car racing simulator can match that for me, and I haven’t even touched the Scenarios and Arcade mode. I haven’t even mentioned the little secrets and surprises, which I won’t spoil. Please make a sequel and don’t change this high-octane recipe! Maybe make eight planets instead of six, if that’s possible. 10/10
